definition: A rule that moves a shape or changes its size, such as a reflection, rotation, translation or enlargement.
The shape you get after a transformation; the shape you started with is the object, and the image of $P$ is often labelled $P'$.
A transformation that flips a shape in a mirror line: each point moves straight across the line, at right angles to it, to the same distance on the other side.
A transformation that turns a shape about a fixed point, the centre, through an angle, clockwise or anticlockwise.
A transformation that slides every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction, given by a column vector.
A transformation that multiplies the move from a fixed centre to every point by the same scale factor, so the image is the same shape but may be a different size.
A quantity with both a size and a direction, such as a move on a grid; it is often written as a column vector.
A vector written as two numbers in a column, $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}$: $x$ across (negative means left) and $y$ up (negative means down).
One transformation followed by another, where the second is applied to the image of the first.
